paragraphs: Hyman describes him as a student of R’ Abbahu. At the beginning of chapter 9 of Jerusalem Talmud Nazir, a gentile woman comes before R’ Abbahu. He tells Avimi bar Tovi, “Go and find her an opening [on the basis of new circumstances].” In Jerusalem Talmud Bava Batra 2:3, R’ Avimi bar Tovi issues a ruling.

notes.text: The consulted Nazir 9:1 paragraph reads בנולד, “on the basis of new circumstances,” where the supplied notice has בגולד. The bracketed English follows that paragraph; Gold is not a person. The notice’s tractate wording is unclear and is not silently rewritten. A separate Nedarim 9:1 check did not locate this account.

The Nazir9:1 account with בנולד is an inherited earlier consultation, not a newly inspected whole primary paragraph. It supports the bracketed basis of new circumstances for opening a vow; supplied בגולד is not a newly identified person Gold. נזכר remains the supplied tractate word beside contextual Nazir9:1, without declaring a printed glyph repair from recurring OCR patterns. The earlier Nedarim9:1 nonmatch is finite. ב״ט expands contextually from Avimi bar Tovi; its BavaBatra2:3 ruling and the personal-title expansions were not newly verified, so R' is retained.

The printed notice (vol. I, p. 88) explicitly names Nazir and reads בנולד. The supplied transcription reads נזכר and בגולד at those points. In Jerusalem Talmud Nazir 9:1, Abbahu directs Avimi bar Tovi to find a basis for releasing the woman from the vow in a new circumstance. Jerusalem Talmud Bava Batra 2:3 names Avimi bar Tovi in a ruling about placing a loom between walls. The student relationship is Hyman’s characterization.
